Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the post-mortem yesterday. GeoFlow's ops team has consolidated the customer impact data and we're asking Redwood for a short-term remediation package. During the 7/28 sustained latency spike (~3 hours), several scheduled customer jobs missed SLAs and a handful of customers were downgraded to batch-only flows.

We're asking for:
- A one-time 20% credit on last month's invoice (July) OR two free service months for the affected product tier;
- Signed amendment that acknowledges the incident timeline and a plan for improved regional routing;

I'm attaching the incident timeline and the internal impact CSV for your reference. Please let me know the path for executive approval and whether a one-time credit is doable versus free months. Carmen (CFO) is looped for procurement.

Best,
Anna

Jordan — I pulled the incident traces and the rego for the regional router. Short summary: the latency spike was triggered by a misrouted batch of long-context requests that bypassed the KV cache for ~2.7 hours. We've got a patch queued that prevents the fallback path and a routing policy change that will reduce exposure for similar traffic patterns. Estimated rollout to production: 3 business days with a canary the next day.

From a technical standpoint, we can commit to an amendment that:
- Documents the incident timeline and root cause;
- Commits to the routing policy change and a canary + full rollout window (3 business days);
- Adds a monitoring hook for GeoFlow's tenant and weekly sync for 30 days post-deploy.

I don't have objections to a concession but recommend credit be usage-tied and capped: e.g., 15% credit on July invoice limited to impacted usage. That keeps the remedy proportional and avoids setting a multi-month precedent.

Karthik

[attachment: geoflow-routing-trace-snippet.txt — excerpted]

Team — commercial take: GeoFlow is a mid-market account with steady growth and a likely expansion in Q4. They are strategic for our regional benchmarks (APAC pilot next quarter). I support a capped, usage-tied credit rather than free months. Proposed offer:

- One-time credit equal to 15% of July bill, applied to next invoice;
- A service credit cap of $45k (whichever is lower between 15% and cap);
- Inclusion of the routing policy commitment and weekly post-deploy sync in the amendment;
- A mutual non-precedent clause (standard legal language) — make it explicit this is a one-time remediation.

For anything >15% or any multi-month concession, I need Lauren/exec signoff. If we keep it at 15% and the cap, I can approve. Please confirm and I'll draft the amendment.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: GeoFlow: request for remediation + credit after 7/28 outage

Thanks for the notes. I appreciate the measured approach. Approve the commercial team's proposed package with these conditions:
1) Credit limited to 15% of July invoice and not to exceed $45k;
2) Amendment must include the routing policy commitment and engineering rollout timeline (3 business days) and be dated;
3) Legal must include a non-precedent clause and we add a reporting cadence;
4) Procurement/CFO acceptance required on GeoFlow's side (we won't auto-apply).

Marissa — proceed to finalize the amendment and send to GeoFlow procurement. Jordan — hold the external communication until the amendment is ready and signed. After signatures, we can process the credit.

Lauren
